utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-32-T, the Prosecutor versus Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Now, sir, would you please take the solemn declaration, which is set out in the card which the Court usher is showing you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sit down, please, sir. The late start this afternoon should not indicate that this is the time we're going to start every afternoon but there were some technical problems with the Court. Yes, Mr. Domazet. Your witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. Examined by Mr. Domazet:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir. I will examine you on behalf of the Defence of Mitar Vasiljevic today; and I would like to advise you not to mention your name and surname, and the number under which you will testify is VGD24. I also kindly ask you that during your testimony, you should mention a person that has also been protected, please use her pseudonym, which will be given to you, which is VG117. You will have before you the name of this person, but please do not pronounce that name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit D48, that we can use again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We have got a new sheet, so that will be Exhibit D49, and it too will be under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. VGD24, we shall begin the examination now, and can you give us some information about yourself, but do not disclose your identity nor your name and surname. First I should like to ask you, where are you currently residing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: VGD24, I live now in [redacted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is your current occupation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I am, at present, a [redacted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old are you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I am [redacted] years old.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the year 1992, where was your place of residence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I lived in Visegrad, in the [redacted], [redacted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the period of May 1992, the time when the Uzice Corps had left the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I remember May. The Uzice Corps left on May 19th or 20th of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were you doing at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I wasn't (redacted). I worked in a chemicals plant, Terpentin. It's a colours and paint factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume that you're referring to the time period until the departure of the Uzice Corps.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do when the Uzice Corps left Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: When they left, I became -- I was mobilised in the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before that period, were you a reserve policeman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No. I had never been a reserve policeman. I was employed in the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From that time onwards, following the departure of the Uzice Corps, you were mobilised in the police in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes. When the Uzice Corps left, a few days later, I was mobilised in the police ranks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was your commander at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: At the time, my commander was Dragan Tomic, who was killed in July or August, I think. He was killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were your duties at the time on that post, your main duty, as far as you can recollect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, there were war conditions then, and I was a reserve police officer, as well as the other police officers. We secured the communications, that is, the roads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the Vuk Karadzic school was in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes, I know where that school is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time you're referring to, at some point in time, were you assigned to secure that school? Was that your duty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes. On one occasion I, together with a colleague, was assigned to secure the school and its surroundings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "with a colleague," do you remember who that colleague was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: His name was Boban Simsic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember when this happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, it was the second half of June. It may have been the 22nd of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Although you are not mentioning the year, I assume you are referring to the year in which you began carrying out this duty.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: When the war broke out in Bosnia and Herzegovina, that was the month of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell me: What do you remember in connection with your assignment that you performed along with Simsic Boban in regard to securing the Vuk Karadzic school in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, we received an oral order from a commander, which I mentioned earlier on. His name was Dragan Tomic. In the mornings, from, let us say, 10.00 in the morning, that we should be present in the vicinity of the Vuk Karadzic school because people of the Muslim ethnicity were to arrive, and that they were to be taken by convoy to places to which these people wished to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told where these Muslims were supposed to come from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: From the area of Zupa, the village of Velika Gostilja, Zep, Kuka. Those are the three villages mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you act on those orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I carried out that duty assigned to me by my commander, Mr. Tomic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you - and when and what time did you - go to that school, and if so, what did you find there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, we went at about 10.00, and we came to the plateau in front of the Vuk Karadzic school. There we found a number, a larger number of women and elderly people. Some of them had already entered the school and others were moving around the plateau -- on the plateau in front of the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion, did you see vehicles which brought these people to the school, or were there no vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: When we came to the spot, there were no vehicles there, but whilst we were going there to the place we were supposed to secure, we encountered three trucks which were going in the direction of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps notice the three trucks and to whom they belonged? Were they military or civilian vehicles? Did they have any markings to be able to see to whom they belonged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, those trucks were not the property of the army but the property of the Centrotrans Visegrad Transport Company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether in those trucks, besides the drivers of their trucks, were there any other people along with the drivers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, in addition to the drivers, there were no other persons in the trucks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you had arrived in front of the school and that you had encountered a large group of people. Some of them were in the school, some of them were still outside the school. In addition to those people, did you perhaps notice some soldiers with them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, there were two soldiers present. One was Ciro Djuric - I think his name is Zoran - and the other was Goran Ristic, and his nickname was Boban.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they wearing uniforms? If so, what sort of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: They were wearing the SMB uniforms of the former Yugoslav army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes, they were armed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Besides the two soldiers you mentioned, did you notice any other soldiers or any other armed person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No. There were no other soldiers wearing uniforms or carrying arms. There may have been some citizens from the neighbourhood, of Serb nationality, who were communicating with those people who had just arrived from Gostilja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What else did you notice?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, nothing in particular was happening. Those that were on the plateau, they eventually entered the school building also.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you well, at the time when you arrived, you said that a part of these people had already entered the school, and while you were still there, the remaining people were also entering the school.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Those who had been on the plateau also entered the school building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While these people were entering the school and finally entered the school building, were you present all the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes. We were present in front, on the plateau, until everyone entered the inside of the building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion, did you notice that someone was recording the names of the people who were entering the school building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No one was present there to write down those names and establish the numerical figures. They were neither in front of the school nor in the school, with the exception of Djuric and Ristic and the policemen and a few women who were talking to the people that had come from Gostilja.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If someone was writing those names down, would you have been in a position to see that, given the place where you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No. The plateau was clean. There were no obstacles there. I could not see anyone there, writing down the names of the people at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice at the entrance a table or some chairs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No. There was nothing there; no objects, no tables, no chairs, no other objects. The plateau was clean. It was covered with asphalt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you told us you were outside the building until the time when everyone went into the school building, how long did you remain after that in front of the school building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, we stayed an hour, perhaps a bit more. Occasionally we visited the neighbourhood and then we would return, and we were in communication with the two soldiers, to see whether there were any problems involved, and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understood you well, at the beginning when you arrived, you stayed there an hour, at least, and then, after that, you would occasionally leave and come back.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes. We stayed, at the first moment, an hour or so, and then we would occasionally leave for short periods of time. We were either in the vicinity of the school or in front of the school building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "for short periods of time," what period of time are you referring to? Can you perhaps assess what the time period was between your departures and returns?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, perhaps 10 or 20 minutes, intervals of 10 or 20 minutes. We would visit the settlement, the area, and then we would return to the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I forgot to ask you at the beginning, I believe: Did you come and visit on foot or by car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: We were on foot. We were a pedestrian patrol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day when you saw these people for the first time, do you remember any incident occurring in respect of those people who were coming or going from the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: While we were present there, and even when we were absent and when we returned, we communicated with the two, Djuric and Ristic, and they informed us that no incidents had occurred on that day in front of the school, in the school, or in the surrounding area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you notice that the people who were accommodated in the school, that some of these people were leaving the school or that other people from outside were coming into the school? Were they able to do so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, all the people that were put up in the school had freedom of movement. This was not restricted in any way. They were visiting their family, their friends, for coffee, and they were waiting for the convoy to come and to take them to the places they wished to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, as far as you could see, how many people were there present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I cannot give you the exact figure, but I would say about a hundred people; men, women. All in all, about a hundred people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you have the list of the witnesses including names and pseudonyms, to tell me whether you see VG117 in front of you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once again, let me ask you to be careful not to mention the name in question. Did you know this person at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I did not know the person by the pseudonym VG117.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if this person was amongst the people whom you described as being at the school at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I learned from Ristic and other soldiers who were there that there was a family from Gostilja there that had a high-ranking officer - a major, I think - serving with the Yugoslav People's Army in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they tell you about her and members of her family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I was told that they had to be taken to Serbia because this officer would be waiting for them there to take them over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who else was with her? Do you know who had come from Gostilja, any other family member?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I don't know exactly who was with her. I just know that there were three or four members of this family that were supposed to travel to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know at the time where other people who had come from Gostilja and other villages, where they were supposed to go? To Serbia as well, or somewhere else within the Federation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, I knew that some had to go to the Federation, some to Uzice. There was a group that was supposed to go to Priboj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether this person, VG117, and members of her family, did indeed leave the school in question and travel to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: While I was there, at that time, while we were patrolling and providing the security for the school building, no, they didn't go on that day. However, I know that two days later they were returned to their village and that Miloje Joksimovic, a neighbour of theirs, took them to Gostilja, from where they continued on foot towards Racunici and further on to Serbia, where they were eventually taken over by this officer, who I think took them to Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember who it was who told you this, that they ended up in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I heard about that at the police station, because everybody knew that this family would be taken to Serbia, that they were supposed to be taken there and that this officer would take them over. I don't know who exactly -- what kind of relationship it was, whether his father was one of the people at the school. I'm not sure about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that it was at the police station that you learned about this. However, you told us that it was Djuric and this other soldier who had told you about this. Does it mean that there were actually two sources of information, that you heard from both of them about this family and that they were to be taken to Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes. I heard this both from Ristic and other people, and also I heard the same story at the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember, by any chance, whether what you were told about this family at the police station took place before they came from Gostilja or only later on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I remember hearing the story about a family that had a son who was serving in Belgrade and that they were supposed to be taken to Serbia, where he would take them over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you spoke about the time period in question, not everything was very clear. Could you be more precise? You said that it was not on the first day. Tell us when it was that they left Visegrad finally. When did they leave the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I think that they spent two nights in the school and then were taken to Miloje Joksimovic's place at Gostilja, who made contact with their son, and I know that they went on foot to Racunici, which is on the border with Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should like to ask you to try to remember when this family, VG117 and members of her family, were taken away, what happened with the remaining people, with this group of people that was at the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I know that they stayed behind, that they spent at least seven or eight days at the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about the way in which VG117's family left the school in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I heard that they had been transported to Gostilja in a Lada Niva, that they were taken to Miloje Joksimovic's house in Gostilja and that, from there, they were taken to Racunici, that is, to the border with Serbia, where they were taken over by this relative of theirs who was a serving member of the military.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Speaking of the remainder of the group which was in the school, the group of people that stayed after this family had left, could you remember whether at any point in time they left the school building in an organised manner? Were there any attempts to transfer them to any other location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes, there were attempts to take them back to their village, their villages, and I know that a number of vehicles were gathered. They were supposed to be taken back to Gostilja. However, from the other side of the Drina, Muslims opened fire, and it was at that moment impossible for them to be returned to their village, so they had to be taken back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say they had to be taken back to the same place, are you referring to the Vuk Karadzic elementary school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes, I am referring to the Vuk Karadzic elementary school, where they were brought initially.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember how many days after their arrival in the school that happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't quite understand your question. Do you mean after the first day they arrived or after this attempt to have them returned to their village failed? Could you repeat that for me, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am referring to the first day when they arrived in the school, in an organised manner. How many days later was this attempt made to take them back to Gostilja?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I believe it took place on the third, the fourth, or maybe the fifth day after their arrival.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you familiar with the reasons why this attempt was made to take them back to Gostilja, in view of the fact that they were supposed to be transferred to other locations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I do remember this moment very well, this period of time very well, because the roads were being endangered by Muslims and it was impossible for them to be taken to these other locations where they wanted to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, aren't we straying a long way away? The issue that the Prosecution was allowed to reopen its case in chief was whether your client was seen pretending to be a member of the ICRC and taking down the names and addresses of people. Now, not even on the widest interpretation of that issue are we in the slightest interested in what happened to these people later, unless it somehow affects that witness's credit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do understand your remark; however, my questions are focused on the examination which was received by -- that is, the questions which we received from VG117. She told us that she was amongst this group of people which was transported to the village; that is, she described the events in a completely different Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. way compared to what the witness is telling us now and compared to what this other witness told us yesterday. My questions go to the issue of credibility of -- and reliability of the testimony of VG117, and I have reasons to doubt her testimony. However, I will be very brief. I'm nearing the end of this part of my examination. I only had a couple of questions left, and I will go back to the relevant issue, that is, the issue of Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: On that rather beguiling promise, Mr. Domazet, you proceed. It really -- as I recall, you raised all this in cross-examination of 117. It was irrelevant then and it seems to me, with all due respect, to be irrelevant now. But you proceed, but please do try to keep to your promise to finish it soon. It isn't of any real assistance at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember, or did you maybe see or hear about any incident taking place after this group was taken back to the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Seven or eight days later, there was an incursion by so-called White Eagles, who allegedly took away their money, their valuables and jewellery and that, after that, they were removed from this building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you personally in the vicinity of the building? Were you providing security to the building or is this something that you only heard from other people subsequently?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No. At that time, I was no longer assigned to this task, but I heard about the incident from my colleagues and some other people around town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one more question regarding this group of people, if you know: Did these people finally leave in an organised convoy; and if not, do you know in what manner they were finally transported from that school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: This group of people that we are now discussing were unable -- that is, it was impossible to transport them because the roads were not safe. So some of them left for Serbia and some were taken to what is today the Federation, that is, the territory which is under the control of Muslim units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I should now like to ask you a few questions about Mitar Vasiljevic. Did you know him at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes, I did know Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How is it that you knew him, and how well did you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I knew Mitar Vasiljevic very well. I knew him as a waiter. He used to work in several catering establishments in Visegrad. I used to see him at the Cadzava restaurant and in the New Hotel, where he worked most of the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you referring to the hotel which is situated in the vicinity of the old bridge in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes. I am referring to the New Hotel, which is located next to the old bridge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you knew him as a waiter. Does it mean that you frequented cafes and restaurants and that that is how you knew him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes. I went to this facility very often. It had a very nice terrace, an open-air terrace, and it was Mitar Vasiljevic who waited on me frequently when he was on duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember in the years preceding the outbreak of the conflict, that is, prior to 1992, where, at what locations, you saw him, if he spent this time working at the same establishment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Mostly I would see him in this New Hotel that I've described. That is where he mostly worked at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one more question regarding that period of time. Are you familiar with the New Hotel at Vilina Vlas, or Banja, near Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with that hotel. There is a large swimming pool there, where I often went to have a swim, not so much to have a drink.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Mitar Vasiljevic working as a waiter in that hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No. Mitar Vasiljevic never worked in that hotel. I may have seen him there as a guest of the hotel, but he was never employed in that establishment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Mitar Vasiljevic well enough so as to recognise him in every situation during those years? Could you be mistaken as to Mitar Vasiljevic in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No, I don't think I could. I really knew Mitar Vasiljevic very well. I've known him for over 20 years. I don't think I could be mistaken when it comes to Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see the individual in question now in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I saw him a moment ago. I cannot see him now because you are in front of me, you are obstructing my view of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for us what he is wearing today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Mitar Vasiljevic is wearing a brown blazer, a white shirt, and a brown tie.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think that does identify the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should now like to go back to 1992, the period of time when you were mobilised into the reserve police force. Do you remember hearing anything about the whereabouts of Mitar Vasiljevic in those days, or did you maybe see him at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, I had an opportunity to see him at the beginning of the conflict. I think I saw him a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you remember? Could you describe for us any such situation in which you saw him personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I remember seeing him once in the Mezalin settlement, cleaning the street with a group of women; the street, the shops, and some business premises there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you happen to notice what he was doing at the time? What was his role?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, he was doing the same thing as this group of people that was with him, these women. They were all cleaning this neighbourhood which is called Mezalin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see him again in a similar situation or in a similar role?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes, I did, a couple more times, in a similar role.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us when this was, approximately, in relation to the time you were mobilised? And you said you were mobilised sometime around the 20th of May. When did you see Mitar Vasiljevic after that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I think it was in early June, at the beginning of the month of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether he wore a uniform or civilian clothes at that time? Do you remember the way he was dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I'm not sure he wore a uniform. I think he wore a dark-coloured suit. Maybe the trousers were olive-drab, but the upper part was darker, maybe black.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On those occasions, did you notice any weapons on him, that is, that he was armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I never saw him armed in town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to notice anything particular in his attire at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes, you're quite right to ask me that question because now I remember noticing a band around his sleeve, indicating that he was cleaning the streets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You used the term -- you said an orderly, that he was an orderly, that he wore a band of an orderly. What does it mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, in my country, it means that during some public manifestations, public events, whenever there is a large group of people gathering, there are individuals who are in charge, and usually they would wear a red band around their sleeve. I don't know whether it was the right sleeve or the left sleeve.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to you, the word "orderly," does it come from the word "order?" Does it mean that those individuals are in charge of maintaining order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, I'm not quite sure. Yes. Those people were there to prevent incidents, to try and see to the public order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just one objection. On the record, page 18, line 14, when the witness said that he noticed an orderly band, the interpretation reads as follows: "... indicating that he was cleaning the streets." I must say that the witness did not use these words. He did not say that he was cleaning the streets but that he wore a band which indicated that he was an orderly, and he just provided us with the explanation as to the meaning of the word "orderly." I don't think the interpretation here was entirely adequate and accurately reflected the words of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, your next question rather supports what you say, because he hadn't mentioned, according to the translation, the word "orderly" before you said, "Well, you've just said orderly." But it doesn't seem to be very important. He's now given us what he said and what he meant by what he said, so I think we can leave it as it stands, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. That was the reason why I asked some additional questions of the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned that the orderly -- this orderly band is usually worn by the people who are in charge of maintaining public order during some public events. Does it mean, according to you, that he was in charge of what was going on at that time in the streets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Most probably he was in charge of the people who were cleaning the streets, the shops, and business premises.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you notice, by any chance, on this band that you said was red, whether there were any other markings or insignia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No. It was a plain red band which had no markings on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you had seen Mitar Vasiljevic on a number of occasions in the month of June. Can you tell us until when he was assigned to that duty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, I saw him performing that duty until mid-June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to him then, in mid-June? Because you say that you were seeing him until then.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: In mid-June, in the streets of the town, he fell from a horse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see that yourself or did you hear about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No. I was not an eyewitness to that, but it was something that was discussed in town. People were laughing about him because he had fallen from a mare and broken his leg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you had heard this from people who were laughing at the incident, can you tell us why would these people laugh at an event in which the person was injured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: It is unusual to ride a horse on the pavement, and people, I suppose, were joking about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion, when you heard of that incident and when you heard about where the event took place and the time of the incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, this happened at the square near the New Hotel, where the Kristal Bank is currently located, and there is a glass there where posters are put up and where information is given.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear when that happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, I heard -- well, people said, in fact, that this happened during an Orthodox holiday, the Trinity Day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us something about the Red Cross in Visegrad. Do you remember, at the time, where the Red Cross premises were located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I remember that very well. The Red Cross premises were located in the second Podrinjeska Street, near the restaurant owned by Boro Sokra [phoen] of Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember who was employed in the Red Cross in Visegrad at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I remember well. Milan Knezevic, nicknamed Bato; a woman called Bugarin - I don't know her surname - and another woman called Stojka were employed at the Red Cross at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether at some point in time a person by the name of Zilic was employed there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes. Stanimir Zilic used to work there. He is a former police officer. Now he's retired. He used to work in the Red Cross, but at some later stage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "at some later stage," at the time we are discussing now, June 1992, he hadn't been working for the Red Cross then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No, he was not employed with the Red Cross at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember, how much later did he become employed with the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly, but I think it was much later that he began working in that institution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Domazet, can I just check the name that he mentioned there?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: He's recorded as saying Milan Knezevic, M-i-l-a-n.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is that what you understood him to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you say Milan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Milan. Milan Knezevic, nicknamed Bato.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It's not Mitar, is what I'm interested in. I thought this might have been --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No, no. Milan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I thought this might have been your alleged doppelganger but you haven't produced him yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The person called Zilic that you mentioned, can you say that he started working with the Red Cross in a few months from then, or even later than that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure when he started working with the Red Cross, but it was later. I don't know the exact time, because he was in fact distributing humanitarian aid; flour, sugar, and the like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember what he looked like? I'm referring to Zilic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I don't really have to remember because I know the person personally and I know exactly what he looks like. He is one metre, 75 centimetres tall, he has dark hair, dark complexion, he's not -- he's averagely developed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From that description, because you say that you knew the person quite well, do you see any similarity between that person and Mitar Vasiljevic, whom you know very well too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: It is certain that there is a lot of similarity in terms of height, colour of hair, complexion, build.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But as far as you can remember, that person was not employed with the Red Cross in June 1992? You are sure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure. I didn't see him there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, I would like to ask you: At the time when you were assigned to the school Vuk Karadzic, did you at any time or in any situation see Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: On that specific day, I didn't notice Mitar Vasiljevic anywhere, standing or moving around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not only on that day, but on previous days, did you see Mitar Vasiljevic in those days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: From the time when he fell off the horse, he was taken to the clinic in Uzice. His leg was fractured. And from mid-June onwards, I didn't see him any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us: From the time when, as you have just explained, that you heard that Mitar Vasiljevic was injured from having fallen from the horse and to the time when you started securing the school, do you know what time interval would that be? Can you remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I will rephrase. Did you hear of the injury of Mitar Vasiljevic before you secured the school Vuk Karadzic or after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: About his injury? Well, I heard about it seven or eight days before I went to secure the school in question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure of that, that this was the time interval, seven or eight or more days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, about a week, seven days.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Groome:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: VGD24, my name is Dermot Groome. I will be asking you several questions on behalf of the Prosecution. You've told us today here that Mitar Vasiljevic worked in the New Hotel by the old bridge and some cafes in town; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct that I said that Mitar Vasiljevic was employed in the catering establishments you just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would that have been in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No, it wasn't in June. It was before the war broke out in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it have been in May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I saw him at the beginning of 1992 and before that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When is the last time you saw him working in establishments that you've described for us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: The last time I saw him working in the Novi Hotel, the New Hotel, which is near the old bridge over the Drina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when would have been the last time you saw him there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: It was in winter, winter of 1992, that is, until the period of spring.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're sure that at no time he worked at the Vilina Vlas hotel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I'm sure that he never worked in Vilina Vlas hotel. I had an uncle there who was employed there and I used to go there quite frequently, and I never met him there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the JNA was in town, where were they staying overnight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the question in regard to the JNA?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the JNA came to Visegrad, where did the officers stay at night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, the JNA arrived on April 16, 17, but where they spent their night, I really do not know. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to be asking this witness about another protected witness, so I'm going to tender at this time document P96. It's a pseudonym sheet for VG81.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is that a document which is already marked 86 -- 96, I mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. It's a new one for the purposes of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It will be Exhibit P96, and it will be under seal. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, VGD24, I'd ask you to look at the sheet in front of you, and that's another witness who is protected, just like yourself, so I'd ask you to refer to her as VG81. You arrested that woman in September of last year, did you not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Personally, I know the person 081, but I never arrested that person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you involved -- did you have any interaction with that person on the 13th of September, 2001?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: It is true that I was on duty on that day and I was there when there was a conflict between VG081 and the wife of the accused, Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do with respect to VG81 with what you're calling a conflict? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I went to the scene, the place called Kosovo Polje, where the person VG081, that is where she lives. I was accompanied by policemen. We questioned the person, we established the facts, and I fined her on the spot of ten convertible marks, which she paid on the spot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you determined, after speaking to which people, that VG81 should be fined? Which people did you interview to determine the facts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I talked with Mitar Vasiljevic's wife and with the person in question, who confirmed that she had a quarrel with the wife of Mitar Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you fine the wife of Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes -- no, I didn't fine Mitar Vasiljevic's wife because VG081 had started the conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're telling us that VG81 was at her home, you were called to go to that home, where you met VG81 and the wife of Mr. Vasiljevic, and after talking to both of them, you determined that VG81 was in the wrong and you fined her; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: That is correct. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you fine her for? What violation of law did you charge her with or fine her for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Because when she was travelling Visegrad to Kosovo Polje in a white Niva Lada, she had stopped by Vasiljevic's wife and she started calling out to her, saying that Mitar Vasiljevic was a war criminal and words to that effect, which she acknowledged when being questioned by me, and I fined her. And she didn't object to that. She took out the necessary amount of money and gave it to me, and I wrote a receipt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that she was a witness, or was scheduled to be a witness in this case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that she was a witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where the village of Kragujevac is? That's K-R-A-G-U-J-E-V-A-C.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I know where Kragujevac is located. That is the town where I was born.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, I would be interested to know what is the crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: It is rather important, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what violation of law or crime was VG81 charged with that she had to pay this fine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, she disrupted public order, and this entails a fine of 10 convertible marks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is there a section or a law that you can tell us, a section number of the law that you specifically charged her with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes, there is a section, provoking another person to quarrel and using offensive language.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the section?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Article 2, para 1.1, as far as I can remember. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what day was that on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: This was last year, autumn last year. I think that you mentioned September 13. I'm not sure about the date, because I, of course, have to punish people on a daily basis, so I cannot remember all these dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're uncertain about the date; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: That is not a significant date. I don't remember him because I have to fine people on a daily basis, for traffic -- breaking traffic rules or for other things, and I cannot really remember all the dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, your recall or powers of recall seemed quite impressive earlier. You were able to tell us that the date that you went to the Vuk Karadzic school was the 22nd of June in 1992, and you were able to tell us that you had heard that some people were going to go to Racunici, and you remembered that they left in a Lada Niva. How were you able to recall with such great detail the events of almost ten years ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: As regards the fines, it is something which the police does every day, and we would have to have a computer to recall that information. But the other incidents are incidents that occur only rarely, every ten years, and that is why one remembers them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it was your testimony that nothing happened at the school, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I didn't testify to the fact that nothing happened there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the day that the White Eagles apparently went to the school and robbed the people there, can you tell us the date that that happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, I said that I hadn't been there on the spot, and I don't remember the exact day, but from the time when these people arrived to that building, that happened seven or eight days later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a person by the name of Milena Pencencic? That's P-e-n-c-e-n-c-i-c.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No. I'm sorry, I'm not sure about the surname. Can you repeat the name and the surname? I didn't quite get it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The surname is Pencencic - and I've spelled it - and the first name is Milena, M-i-l-e-n-a.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I know a family in Visegrad, a family called Pencencic. Whether the person's name is Milena or not, I'm not sure. I know the family Pencencic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that you were mobilised into the reserve police force, but prior to being mobilised into the reserve police force, you were not a member of the reserve police force; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: That is correct. I wasn't a member of the reserve police before then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in 1993 you joined the police force officially; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes. In 1993 I had completed a course in Bileca, a three-month course, and then I became a regular police officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, can you tell us how it was you were notified that you were mobilised into this reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I was informed by messenger.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was the messenger a police officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I don't think he was a policeman. No, he was not a policeman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: About how many people were mobilised in a similar way, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I'm not sure what the exact number of people who were mobilised. About a hundred. I don't think there were more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that they were all Serb?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: It is true they were all Serbs, because war had broken out in our area. The Muslims had formed their own units, the Serbs had formed their own units, and that was what the situation was at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the date that you were mobilised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I cannot remember the exact date. About 20th, 21st, or 22nd, one of those three days when the Uzice Corps left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the date when you were sworn in as a police officer in 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: In July, the first half of July. 15th of July, 17th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How soon after you were mobilised as a reserve police officer were you issued a weapon? Was it the same day, the next day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: When I reported to the police station, it was then that I was issued with weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long were you at the police station before you were issued with a weapon? An hour, two hours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, as soon as I arrived; 10 or 20 minutes. In that period of time, in those 10 or 20 minutes, I was issued with a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, would this be a convenient place to pause?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Very well. We'll adjourn now until 4.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stanimir Zilic, you've described him as looking somewhat similar to Mr. Vasiljevic. What I'd ask you: Do you think it's reasonably possible that some people might mistake Stanimir Zilic for Mitar Vasiljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: It's true that I have described Stanimir Zilic as looking similar to Mitar Vasiljevic. As to whether one could confuse the two, I don't know. That really depends on the observer. It is true that they resemble each other by their hair, the complexion, the height and the build, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever mistaken one for the other?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, sometimes I am mistaken about people when I see someone resembling some other individual that I know, and at that particular moment I might be mistaken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you about these two specific people. Have you ever gone up to Stanimir Zilic and said, "Hello, Mitar. Oh, I'm sorry, I've made a mistake." Have you ever made that kind of mistake with Mr. Zilic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I did not have an opportunity to make such a mistake, I personally. I saw them on a regular basis almost every day, so I didn't have that opportunity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I believe you said, when you described Mr. Zilic, you said that he was retired now. So can I take from that that he is in his 60s or perhaps older?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No. He's a relatively young man, the same age as Mitar Vasiljevic, more or less. But he retired earlier than usual because of health problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does Mr. Zilic still live in Visegrad today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes. He is still alive and he is residing in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you bring a photograph of Mr. Zilic with you when you came to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No, I did not. There was no need for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know what village Mr. Zilic was born in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Excuse me, who do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stanimir Zilic. Do you know whether he was born in the town of Visegrad or was he born in one of the villages around Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I think that his parents come from Rudo originally. I don't know exactly where he was born, but I think that he originally comes from the municipality of Rudo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, from what you've told us before the break, it seems that the first thing that happened when you arrived at the police station in response to this mobilisation was that you were issued your weapons. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. That is what I testified. I was issued a weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for us what weapons you were issued.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I was issued an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a young man, did you do compulsory military service with the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes. I did my compulsory military service with the Yugoslav national army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this the same type of rifle that you were issued when you did your service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes. I had the same kind of rifle, an automatic rifle, M-70.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any markings on the rifle to indicate that it was a police rifle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Weapons usually don't have any markings that would indicate the type of formation that usually uses that kind of weapon. No, it didn't have any specific markings, just M-70.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Boban Simsic, was he a reserve police officer as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes, he was a reserve police officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever issued a uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Correct, yes, I was also issued a uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when were you issued a uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Sometime later than the rifle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it a matter of days or weeks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Several days, maybe up to two weeks later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during this up-to-two-week period, did you walk around the town with your weapon in your ordinary civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No. I was not wearing civilian clothes, because I already had an old JNA uniform at home. Every male in our country who had done a military service with the JNA had one uniform at home in case of mobilisation or training, things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you issued an identification card?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: At that time, no, we were not issued with any such thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long before you were issued with an identification card to show that you were a police officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: After I completed my training, police training, in Bileca, and when we went back to the police station, we were issued by the Public Security Service a certificate that we were members of the police force, that we were police officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where is Bileca? Is that in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No. Bileca cannot be in Visegrad. It is situated in southern Herzegovina, near the town of Trebinje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, some witnesses have described some of the checkpoints, police checkpoints, around town. As a reserve police officer, were you ever assigned to man one of the checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes, of course I was. I was manning the checkpoints. But I don't know which period of time you have in mind, peacetime or wartime. Could you please repeat the question for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about the time after you were mobilised, and let's confine ourselves just up until the end of June of 1992, during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you assigned to work on checkpoints during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I was assigned, for instance, to the checkpoint in Dobrun.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever assigned to work in the checkpoint on the road out of Visegrad to Prelovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No, never, nor was there a checkpoint there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was no checkpoint on the road from Visegrad in the vicinity of Kosovo Polje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Not the one that would have belonged to our police. It is possible that there was a checkpoint there while the Uzice Corps was still present in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever wear a balaclava during the course of your duties as a reserve police officer? And by that, I mean a cloth covering over your face.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No, never. I never wore any such mask except for a regular cap.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you ever in possession of such a mask?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No, I was never in possession of such a mask. The only thing I had was a regular military beret.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, VG117 has described for us a certificate of safety that was issued to her by your commander, Dragan Tomic. Are you familiar, or were you familiar with such certificates of safety?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I'm personally not familiar with such certificates. They would have been the responsibility of the commander. I was a simple policeman. I was not aware of any such certificates being distributed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, in the course of your duties as a police officer during this time, was it not one of your responsibilities to check the identification papers of people who you saw on the street and perhaps did not recognise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: It is one of the regular duties, obligations, of any police officer on duty. When they see an unknown individual in town, they have to establish his or her identity by asking him identification papers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the course of doing this, you never saw anybody produce a certificate of safety, some certificate verifying who they were, issued by Dragan Tomic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No, I didn't have an opportunity to see that, because most of the time, I was outside the town, not in town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar where the fire brigade building is in the town of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes, I know where the fire brigade is located.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And isn't it a fact that, at different times during this period, Muslims stayed in the fire brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Which period of time do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, May and June of 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No, I don't know that. The only thing I know about is the Vuk Karadzic school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were at the Vuk Karadzic school, did you ever see anybody from the Red Cross at the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No, I never saw anybody from the Red Cross coming to the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Red Cross in Visegrad have another location where they would allow people to stay, people who needed shelter? Was there another place in the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with any such information. The premises of the Red Cross are very small indeed, and they were used as storage room, and it was not possible to accommodate any larger group of people there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's been some testimony in this trial about people being interrogated by police. Can you tell us what locations you are aware of where people were brought for questioning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I'm not aware of the police conducting any such investigations or interrogating people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, then, let me go back to a question I asked you a few minutes ago. If you saw a person, let's say a man whom you did not recognise in the town, and you asked him to identify him testify and he could not produce identification, what would you do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I would have to establish the identity of the individual in question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But if he has no papers to prove who he is, he gives you a name, what would you do, or what would you have done?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I would have to take him to the office of the police, that is, to the police station, and to conduct an interview with him in order to establish who he is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the police station the only place that you're aware of where people were brought to be interviewed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: In the course of our regular work, whenever I came across an unidentified individual, I had to take him to the police station to establish his identity if he didn't have any identification papers on him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What would happen at the police station if he had no identification papers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, his identity would have to be established through an interview, and then it depends on the place where he comes from. We would have to contact the relevant police station, depending on his place of residence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us, approximately how many times during this period of time did you conduct such interviews of people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I never had an opportunity to come across an individual who didn't have any identification papers on him. Most of the time, the people would have some kind of identification; a regular ID, driver's licence, a passport, or some other kind of official document with his picture on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at any time participate in the interview of a person who was perhaps detained by another police officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No. I never had an opportunity to interview an individual which had been brought by another police officer. Usually, the police officer who brought the person to the police station would conduct this activity until the end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Djuric yesterday described for us, at least on one occasion, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. seeing some men who he believed to be paramilitaries in the town. Did you ever see, in the course of your police duties, people that you believed to be paramilitaries in the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I did see such people on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe for us the earliest period of time when you began to see such people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Immediately after the breakout of the conflict in Bosnia and Herzegovina, in particular, in Visegrad, I started seeing such individuals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see White Eagles there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Whether they were White Eagles or Black Eagles, I don't know. All I know is that I saw, from time to time, unknown individuals wearing camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you ever become aware that they had committed crimes in the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I didn't hear anything in particular about them having committed serious crimes, except for what I have mentioned, when they broke into the Vuk Karadzic school and took the money belonging to those people, and similar things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me about the other similar things that you were aware of. About how many other incidents were you aware of that paramilitaries had been involved in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I don't know of any specific similar incidents that would have involved paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Can you tell me, sir, whether they were ever fined 10 convertible marks for interrupting public order?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Probably not, never. There was war going on at that time, and the police was very rarely actually engaged in normal police work. Most of them were at the front lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know a person by the name of Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes, I know the person you're mentioning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you consider yourself a friend of his?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Not really. I don't think I can say that I'm a friend of his, but we are acquaintances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us under what circumstances you are acquainted with Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I knew him even before the outbreak of the war because he comes from a neighbouring village, and I would see him from time to time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see him during this period, between May and June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I cannot recall exactly when that was, but from June onwards, I would see him from time to time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a member of the police force, like yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No. He was never a member of any police force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a member of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: He was not a member of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you saw him during this time period, was he armed with a weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him with a weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would he not fit into your category of paramilitaries, somebody who doesn't belong to any registered force?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Most probably he did belong to a paramilitary formation, because he was neither a member of the police nor Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many people were in his group that you are aware of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: It was not possible for me to know how many people were in his group. I was mostly in charge of securing the roads, and I would rarely go to town. But when I did go to town, I would sometimes see him, but that's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you would see him, would he be alone or with other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Sometimes he was alone, sometimes he was in the company of some other individuals that I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these other individuals that you didn't know, would they be armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Yes, they were all armed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you ever go up to one of these other individuals who you did not know and ask them to produce identification?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, a moment ago I said that the police very rarely did usual police work at that time. Most of the time, they were in charge of securing the roads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us a moment ago that you never had occasion to stop somebody who you did not know and ask for identification. Can I take from that answer that you did not approach any of these unknown individuals that were armed, that were with Milan Lukic, and ask them to identify themselves to you? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, I said that I didn't spend much time in town, that we were basically engaged in securing roads, that we were in the trenches and on the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not asking you about the time when you were out of town. I'm asking you to tell us what you've -- you've described a time, at least one occasion, in which, while you were in town, you saw these unknown men. I'm asking you: On that occasion, did you attempt to identify those men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No. I never tried to ask for their ID, nor was that my duty, nor did I have orders to do so from my commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've heard from a number of witnesses that, during this time period, it was common to see bodies in various parts of the town, as well as buildings burning. Can you describe for us what you recall regarding either bodies on the ground or any signs of violence in the town during this time period.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: I wasn't able to see bodies in the streets or similar locations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So during this entire time period, you never saw any corpses in the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: No. I never had the occasion to see corpses in the town, at least, as far as I was concerned, I wasn't able to see them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often would you receive instructions from your commander, Mr. Tomic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, when we were going to perform our duties, we would receive instructions and orders from our commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can I take from your answer that, every day, Dragan Tomic addressed you and gave you instructions on what you were to do that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VGD24
utterances.text: Well, in most cases, he himself or his deputy or associate would instruct us what we would have to do when we were going to perform our duties, when we were to go to the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during this time period, did Dragan Tomic or his deputies at any time say to you or the other police officers: "I've received a report that Milan Lukic has killed some men down by the Drina River.
